name: OpenCode Observatory
tagline: Self-hosted, metadata-only telemetry and analytics for OpenCode
description:
A self-hosted observability stack for OpenCode. A plugin captures token, model, latency, tool and error metadata; a collector stores it in PostgreSQL; and a React dashboard and read-only MCP server expose usage across machines and tenants. Prompt text, responses, code and provider credentials are excluded by default, with opt-in transcript capture that is scrubbed client-side before anything leaves the process.

The server implements tenant isolation through PostgreSQL row-level security, hourly rollups maintained by statement triggers, an offline SQLite outbox in the plugin, and a historical importer for legacy sessions without double counting. The MCP surface exposes usage summaries, time series, model comparisons, session transcripts and a bitemporal knowledge vault built from summarized sessions.
purpose: To answer where tokens, time and money go across multiple OpenCode machines and accounts without uploading prompts, code or provider credentials to a third party.
strengths: Captures metadata only by default and scrubs opt-in transcripts for tokens, keys and .env assignments before storage
Partitions every tenant query through PostgreSQL row-level security
Uses a durable SQLite outbox so telemetry never blocks or slows inference streams
Normalizes provider token counters and reports prompt-cache reuse and estimated API savings
Combines hourly rollups with exact boundary facts for charts from one hour to several months
Exposes usage, session, error and knowledge-vault queries through read-only MCP tools
Imports legacy sessions with transactional checkpoints and no double counting
Ships a Docker Compose deployment with persistent PostgreSQL and vault volumes
limitations: Self-hosted and OpenCode-specific; there is no public demo instance
Requires PostgreSQL plus a separately built plugin and web/server stack
Transcript capture and model-generated summaries are opt-in and depend on available models
Pricing catalogs need maintenance as providers release or rename models
Tenant isolation depends on a correctly configured reverse proxy and deployment
installation:
# Build the monorepo and generate local secrets
npm install
npm run build
npm run setup:env

# Set ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env, then start PostgreSQL and the app
docker compose up -d --build

# Open http://localhost:7692, sign in and create a telemetry API key (obs_...)
usage:
# Add the plugin to ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["github:chrisb09/opencode-observatory#v0.2.0"]
}

# Or connect from inside an OpenCode session:
# "Connect to Observatory at http://localhost:7692 with key obs_..."

# Query usage from the MCP tools: usage_summary, usage_timeseries, list_sessions
roadmap: Expand provider pricing coverage and audit models without a market-rate match
Continue hardening multi-tenant deployment, backups and reverse-proxy defaults
Improve session-memory and vault extraction quality
Add more deployment examples for LAN and hosted setups
